hook: Build a song from section blocks A, B, C and D. Change one note in A and every A in the song changes with it, so AB, ABA and rondo become shapes you can see and hear. Then label six well-known songs by ear.
outcome: Organize short musical sections into forms (AB, ABA, AABA, rondo), refine them, and hear how repetition and contrast shape a song
sources: National Core Arts Standards, Music (MU:Cr2, MU:Cr3, MU:Re7): https://www.nationalartsstandards.org/
Form names (strophic, through-composed, binary, ternary, rondo): Britannica, "Musical form", https://www.britannica.com/art/musical-form ; Britannica, "Rondo", https://www.britannica.com/art/rondo
AABA as a common popular song form (32-bar form): Open Music Theory, "AABA (32-bar song form)", https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/
Ode to Joy: Beethoven, Symphony No. 9, finale (1824), public domain score at IMSLP, https://imslp.org/wiki/Symphony_No.9,_Op.125_(Beethoven,_Ludwig_van)

Twinkle Twinkle ("Ah! vous dirai-je, maman", France, 1761), Mary Had a Little Lamb (words by Sarah Josepha Hale, 1830; traditional tune), Row Row Row Your Boat (1881), Hot Cross Buns and Frere Jacques (traditional): public domain melodies as sung in US music classrooms, checked against the Library of Congress Songs of America pages, https://www.loc.gov/collections/songs-of-america/
Starter songs written for Curio Class; all sounds are made in the browser
